title: Is It Really You?
release: Is It Really You? (Collaborative Single with Loathe)
era_role: Non-album collaborative single (originally by Loathe from 'I Let It in and It Took Everything', 2020, reinterpreted by Sleep Token in 2022). Categorized among standalone singles as it lacks a Sundowning sigil or TPWBYT oceanic depth, yet remains thematically aligned with oneiric skepticism ('Is it really you?').
in_character_quotes_gap_reason: Sleep Token granted very few interviews in 2016-2018 and never provided track-by-track in-character commentary.

editorial_reading.summary: Collaboration celebrated by the British metal press as the meeting of the two most atmospheric forces in the modern UK scene: Vessel transforms Loathe's shoegaze composition into a gospel-ambient prayer.
editorial_reading.source_title: Louder - The story behind every Sleep Token song

editorial_reading.summary: Early on in the year, they were a supporting act for Loathe and Holding Absence.[17] In April they performed at Maida Vale Studios for the BBC Radio 1 Rock Show with Daniel P. Carter.[18] In June they played at Camden Rocks Festival.[19]

The band have been vague, simply crediting "a plethora of artists" as inspiration.[8] Early in their career, though, they did name Leprous, Agent Fresco, Bon Iver, Meshuggah[131] and Failure as influences.[132] In 2023, II cited British electronic music, drum and bass, Matt McDonaugh from Mudvayne, Joey Jordison of Slipknot, Derek Roddy of Nile, Hate Eternal and Malevolent Creation and Eric Moore, live drummer for Bobby Brown and Suicidal Tendencies, as his main influences.[133] Commentators have also posited performers such as Casey,[134] Loathe,[135] Deftones, Cult of Luna, Explosions in the Sky and Ólafur Arnalds as possible influences.[130][136][137]
